---
title: A client per conversation
description: mcpClientPool() keeps one MCP client per authenticated conversation for one server — opened once, bounded, never closed while a call is in flight, and ended remotely with the outcome reported.
---

> A `'reuse'` session keeps a server warm for one conversation. That only works
> when every conversation has an MCP client of its own. `mcpClientPool()` builds,
> finds, bounds and ends those clients, so a host serving many people does not
> have to.

## When to use it

Use a pool when an MCP server keeps state per session and you serve more than one
person: AgentCore Runtime with `session: 'reuse'`, or any stateful Streamable HTTP
server. One `mcpClient` shared by everyone puts every user in one session. A
client per run pays the cold start on every turn and leaves a session behind
whenever a run throws.

For a stateless server, the default `'per-call'` session and a plain `mcpClient`
are enough.

## One pool per server

Pass a function of the identity as `transport`: each client then gets a transport,
and a session map, of its own.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="pool" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: pool)" />

An agent takes the pool's `toolProvider()`. Each iteration it lists that
conversation's tools, bound to it. A bound tool takes a lease on its
conversation's client for one call, opening the client first when the
conversation has none. Nothing is held between calls.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="agent" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: agent)" />

The client is keyed by the identity the **caller** named in `run({ identity })`.
A run that named none is refused (`no-identity`), because an identity derived
from a session id is not an authenticated one. A missing `principal` is refused
unless you pass `requirePrincipal: false`; pass `requireTenant: true` on a
multitenant host. Verify the caller at your door before you name the identity.

## Tool lists: per client, unless you declare a share

By default each conversation lists its own client's tools, and that list belongs
to one client. A replacement client lists again, and a tool bound to the old
client is sent only if the new list holds the same definition.

When you know that conversations see the same list, say so. The pool checks the
transport's own configuration too, and never shares across tenants.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="share" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: share)" />

Never share a server whose list changes as a session goes on. Every list stops
being served after `pool.permissionsChanged({ tenant, principal? })`,
`pool.toolsChanged()`, the server's own tools-changed notice, or
`definitionTtlMs`. A tool bound to it is then refused (`stale-tools`) before
anything is sent.

`share` is asked again at every listing and every call, so a version in the
`authorization` name works for conversations that already have a client too.
When the name changes, the next listing lists again under the new name. A tool
bound under the old name is refused (`binding-changed`) before it is sent, even
if nothing was listed since. Keep `share` synchronous and cheap.

A list is kept only under the names it was listed for. The pool asks again
when the listing is sent and when its answer arrives. If the names changed in
between, the answer is dropped and the pool lists again under the new names,
so one role's tools are never kept, or served, under another's.

## Full means refused, never queued

Three budgets apply: open clients (`maxClients`, and `maxClientsPerPrincipal`),
clients being ended (`maxEnding`), and operations outstanding on any client
(`maxOperations`). An operation stays charged until its work has settled, not
just until its caller timed out. When a budget is full, `PoolFullError` comes at
once, and its `limit` names the budget.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="full" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: full)" />

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="ending" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: ending)" />

A client in use is never evicted, closed for idleness or ended. That includes
the moment just after it opens, before the caller that opened it has its
lease. To keep a conversation's client through a whole turn, hold
`pool.acquire(identity)` around `agent.run()` and `release()` it after (it is
`AsyncDisposable`). An `acquire` still waiting when the pool closes is refused
(`closed`) and holds nothing.

## Ending a conversation

`pool.terminate({ tenant, principal, conversationId? })` ends the remote session
and reports what the server answered. `close()` on a client ends only the local
side; `terminate()` ends the remote session, and says whether it did.

<CodeFile path="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts" region="terminate" title="examples/features/120-mcp-client-pool.ts (region: terminate)" />

`resolved` is `true` only for `'terminated'`, `'already-gone'` and `'no-session'`.
After `'not-offered'`, `'failed'`, `'timed-out'` or `'handle-lost'`, the remote
session lives until the server's own timeout; `stats().unresolvedEndings` counts
those. On AgentCore Runtime under `'reuse'`, an ending is `StopRuntimeSession`.

`terminate()` answers within its deadline even when a client's local close
hangs, and the deadline is elapsed time: a clock change does not stretch it.
The ending keeps its ending slot and its operation slot until that close
really finishes, and `settled()` waits for it.

## What the record says

In a run, every listing and every call through the pool files one
`agentfootprint.tools.mcp_client` event: the server, `at` (`'list'` or
`'call'`), the client it touched (`opened`, `joined`, `reused`, `not-needed`,
`refused`, `expired`, `handle-lost`), why a replacement opened (`previous`), a
refusal's word, and the conversation as `keyHash`, a short digest. It never
carries an identity value, a session id, an argument or a result.

Outside a run, endings, deferred endings, revoked leases and work that settled
after its caller was answered reach your `onEvent` as an `McpPoolReport`
(`kind`, `reason` — an `McpPoolEndReason` — the remote outcome, `durationMs`).
`stats()` returns an `McpPoolStats`: counts only, including the work still
charged past its deadline (`unsettled`) and the endings never confirmed
(`unresolvedEndings`).

## Nothing is sent unchecked

Every pooled request is checked against its tool's binding before it leaves:
when the SDK sends it, when the pool's `fetch` hands it on, before each retry,
after a credential arrives, and after AWS signing. The pool refuses what it
cannot check:

- A transport whose `send` cannot be watched is never opened. The listing or
  call fails with `init-failed`, and nothing is sent.
- A request that carries no guard is refused unsent (`request-unmatched`).
  For example, an SDK that rebuilt a tool call's params without its marker, so
  the pool could not tie the call to its tool.

`replay` (who may send a call again, `McpClientOptions.replay`) is passed to
every client and works as on a standalone client. It never turns the check off.

## Gotchas

- **Two failures that look alike stay two.** A server's 404 for the session it
  issued is `SessionExpiredError`. A handle this process lost is
  `LocalSessionHandleLostError`, and nothing was sent. Neither call is repeated;
  the next one opens a new client for the same conversation. The lost client's
  local close still counts: it holds an ending slot until it finishes.
- **The budgets bound client objects, endings and operations.** They do not bound
  response sizes or total memory. Put per-caller limits at your door
  (`AdmissionPolicy`).
- **The pool lives in one process.** Send `permissionsChanged` to every process,
  or put a version in the `authorization` name you declare.
- **No timer is installed.** Idle clients are ended at the next pool call, or when
  you call `pool.sweep()`. Set `idleMs` below your runtime's idle timeout.

## What the package exports

From `agentfootprint/providers`:

| export | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `mcpClientPool(options)` | Build a pool for one server. Returns an `McpClientPool`. |
| `McpClientPoolOptions` | `name`, `transport` (or a function of the identity), the budgets, `initTimeoutMs`, `idleMs`, `maxLeaseMs`, `definitionTtlMs`, `definitions`, `requirePrincipal`, `requireTenant`, `onEvent`, and the connection options passed to every client (`resultMode`, `clientInfo`, `retryOnThrottle`, `replay`, `sdk`, `jsonSchemaValidator`). |
| `MCP_POOL_DEFAULTS` | The defaults: 64 clients, 8 per principal, 8 endings, 256 operations, a 30 s open, 600 s idle, a 15-minute lease, a 600 s definitions limit. |
| `MAX_DEFINITION_ENTRIES` | At most this many shared definition entries are kept (256). |
| `MAX_SHARED_TOOLS` | A list longer than this (512 tools) is used by its own client and never shared. |
| `McpPoolDefinitionSharing` / `McpPoolShareContext` | `definitions: { share }`, and the `configuration` and `authorization` names `share` returns. |
| `McpPoolIdentity` | `{ tenant?, principal?, conversationId }`, the conversation a client is for. |
| `McpPoolScope` | What `terminate` and `permissionsChanged` name. |
| `McpPoolLease` | What `acquire` returns: `tools()`, `release()`, and `AsyncDisposable`. |
| `McpPoolStats` / `McpPoolReport` / `McpPoolEndReason` | Counts, the reports `onEvent` receives, and why a client ended. |
| `PoolFullError` / `McpPoolLimit` | A full budget, refused at once: `limit` is `'pool'`, `'principal'`, `'ending'` or `'operations'`. |
| `McpPoolRefusedError` / `McpPoolRefusal` | A refusal before the call was sent: `reason`, `sent: false`. |
| `canTerminate(client)` / `TerminableMcpClient` | Can a client end its remote session? |
| `McpTerminateOutcome` | What ending a session came to. |
| `McpTransportSettings` | A transport's comparable settings as data (`McpHttpTransport.settings`). |

From `agentfootprint`: `SessionExpiredError` (a server ended the session) and
`LocalSessionHandleLostError` (this process lost the handle; nothing was sent).
